head_commit.message:
docs: stop claiming zero telemetry now that crash reporting ships (#954)

ADR-0020 added Sentry crash reporting (desktop, default ON, opt-out), which reversed a published
"no telemetry" promise. The prose in README.md and SECURITY.md was rewritten at the time, but three
summary claims were missed and kept asserting the old promise:

- README.md Privacy bullet — ~70 lines below the paragraph that correctly names Sentry, in the
  same file, so the README contradicted itself.
- The landing home page's "Privacy-first" card.
- branding/marketing/build.mjs — sub-headline and pill, which pair it with "run 100% offline",
  so the two claims compounded. The rendered 04-private-ai.png is regenerated to match; the other
  three slides re-rendered byte-identical, so no font or renderer drift.

All three now say "no analytics" and name the opt-out crash report, matching the /privacy page and
the "Crash reporting" vocabulary entry in docs/CONTEXT.md.

Left alone deliberately: the two extension-scoped claims. The extension is excluded from Sentry and
declares data_collection_permissions ['none'] to Firefox AMO, so "no telemetry" is true there and
load-bearing for that filed declaration.

Adds check 6 to scripts/check-landing-drift.mjs: a denylist for "zero/no telemetry" over README.md,
SECURITY.md, branding/ and the landing source, scanning by root rather than an explicit file list so
a new marketing surface is covered when it lands. Allowlists the extension privacy section and the
tech-radar entry, whose rationale narrates the reversal rather than claiming it. Verified
non-vacuous: reintroducing the phrase in README.md fails the check.

Corrects two claims in ADR-0020's Consequences section. It said README, SECURITY.md, ARCHITECTURE.md
and CONTEXT.md "were rewritten in the same change" — the rewrite was incomplete. It also credited
check-parity.mjs and check-landing-drift.mjs with failing the build when code and copy disagree;
neither mentioned Sentry or telemetry, and check-parity is a copy-preservation gate that cannot tell
a surviving phrase from a true one. There was no mechanical guard at all, which is why it drifted.

head_commit.message:
feat: add the cologne navy resume template and a shared navy letter layout (#953)

* feat: add the cologne navy resume template and a shared navy letter layout

Ports the supplied Cologne Navy design into the Typst backend as a 13th
template, plus a fourth cover-letter layout in matching styling.

Three of the brief's assumptions did not hold against this codebase, and each
changed the work:

Carlito is ALREADY bundled, and `FontFamily::Calibri` already resolves to it in
Typst — the metric-compatible substitution the brief asks for is the repo's
existing convention, so the "check whether it's bundled, add it if not" step was
already satisfied.

Letter templates are NOT per resume template. There are three shared layouts
behind a `LetterLayout` enum, chosen independently of the resume template. So
this adds a FOURTH shared layout, offered to every template and inheriting
whichever palette is active — a Regent user selecting Navy gets Regent's
burgundy. Confirmed as the intent before building it.

`base` as a per-template size option conflicts with the model here: `_scale.typ`
is a locked shared house scale and the only per-template knobs that reach a
template are page size, accent, lang, ats and has_photo. The design's
"everything is a multiple of base" property is preserved as ratios off body_pt;
adding a real size option would be a pipeline change across all thirteen
templates, not a template addition.

The reference also consumed its own rich schema (skills groups, project
stack/links, footnotes rows). This repo has ONE generic IR every template
shares, so what is ported is the LOOK, not the schema — the same way meridian
and throughline style identical `sections[].blocks[]` differently. Nothing was
invented and no section dropped.

DEVIATION worth reading: the brief's 0.14em name / 0.18em heading tracking makes
the PDF text extract letter-by-letter — the name came back as
"À LVA R O   È S P O S I T O" and headings as "S U M M A R Y". For a
job-application tool that is an ATS-unreadable name, not a cosmetic issue.
Reduced to 0.06em / 0.10em, the widest values that still extract, and inside the
0.03–0.10em band every other template here already uses. Caught by the
every-template extraction test, which fails at the brief's values.

Also fixes three stale counts found while wiring this up, all unnoticed because
the generators are ignored by CI: the cover-preview generator asserted 10 files
against a 12-entry list (so it could not be run at all), the showcase banner
hardcoded COLS=12 and panicked with an out-of-bounds pixel write on a 13th cell,
and both printed hardcoded counts in their success messages. All now derive from
the canonical list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop the navy letter rendering as banded in docx, and unhardcode its tracking

Five review findings.

The DOCX letter renderer branched on a single `is_refined` boolean, so Navy fell
into the else and inherited BANDED's decoration — the shaded header band and the
short rule footer, neither of which the Navy design has. The same export
therefore produced a Navy PDF and a Banded DOCX. Split out `is_banded` for the
two branches that are genuinely Banded-only, and gave Navy its own centred
letterhead over a bottom rule, which is the parser-safe echo of the .typ. The
branches Navy legitimately shares with Banded (uppercase name, bolded
date/recipient) stay on `!is_refined` rather than being duplicated.

Navy had no DOCX coverage at all. It now joins the three enumerated loops
(font-size ceiling, letterhead-less, subject-line) and the distinct-bytes test,
where the load-bearing pair is Navy vs Banded — that assertion fails against the
old boolean.

`cologne_navy.typ` set fonts as bare strings while every other template, its own
PR sibling included, uses a fallback tuple. Given fallbacks are how the bundled
Carlito is reached in the first place, that was a real gap, not a style nit.

`heading_tracking: 0.18` in the registry was both dead and wrong — the template
hardcoded 0.10em. The template now reads the field and the registry says 0.10,
so the source of truth is single and the extraction constraint is recorded where
someone changing it will look.

And the tier-badge test asserted only an aggregate count, which would still pass
if a different card supplied the eighth ATS badge and cologne-navy were missing
entirely. Added an assertion naming the card.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: route every navy docx branch by feature, not by "not refined"

The review was right that my first pass was partial, and finishing it found two
more mismatches it had not named.

I split only the header band and the footer rule and left the rest binary, so
Navy still lost Refined's role line and subject caption and still inherited
Banded's bolding. My own commit message claimed Navy "legitimately shares the
bolded date/recipient" with Banded — that was wrong, and checking
letter_navy.typ would have shown it: its emit-date-block and
emit-recipient-block carry no `weight: "bold"`, unlike letter_banded.typ's. I
asserted a justification instead of reading the template I had just written.

Replaced the boolean with per-FEATURE flags derived from what each `.typ`
actually renders — shows_title, shows_subject_caption, bolds_addressing — so a
future layout has to state its behaviour rather than inherit Banded's by
default.

Two further mismatches found while auditing the remaining branches:

The contact line was right-aligned unconditionally, so Navy's centred letterhead
was centred name over a right-aligned contact.

And the letterhead rule sat on the NAME paragraph, drawing a line between the
name and its own contact line. letter_navy.typ rules under the whole block
(name → title → contact), so it belongs on the contact paragraph.

The new test asserts the FEATURES rather than "differs from Banded" — no shaded
band, centred letterhead, fewer bold runs than Banded. "Differs from Banded"
passes as soon as one branch is split, which is exactly how the first pass
looked complete. Verified to fail against the single-boolean version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: make each letter layout state its docx style instead of inheriting

Third review round on this function, so patching a fourth branch was the wrong
answer.

The finding was real: the no-profile FALLBACK contact path still right-aligned
Navy with no rule, while the profile-backed path centred it and ruled it. The
same letter rendered differently depending on whether a ContactProfile happened
to be attached.

The cause is structural, not a missed line. A single `is_refined` boolean with
everything else falling through to Banded meant adding a layout inherited
Banded's look by DEFAULT, and each review round found a different survivor:
round one the header band and footer rule, round two the title, subject caption
and bolding, round three this contact path.

Replaced it with a `LetterDocxStyle` filled in per layout — uppercase name, name
size bonus, header band, centred letterhead, title, subject caption, addressing
bold, header rule, footer rule, signature gap, and the two spacing values. Every
call site reads a field, and both contact paths call one `contact_align()` so
they cannot drift apart again. A new layout now fails to compile until someone
states what it does.

The test was weak in the same way the code was: `contains("center")` passed
while the fallback contact was still right-aligned, because centring the NAME
alone satisfied it. It now counts centred and right-aligned paragraphs and
requires at least two centred — verified to fail against the pre-fix fallback.

Behaviour for Classic, Refined and Banded is unchanged; their table entries were
read off the existing branches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: style navy's docx title and caption from its own typ, not refined's

Both findings are the same defect as the last three rounds, one level down: the
style struct made each feature's PRESENCE layout-aware and left its STYLING
hardcoded to Refined's.

So Navy rendered the role line accent-coloured, uppercased and letter-spaced
while letter_navy.typ puts it in the muted date colour, plain case, untracked;
and the subject caption in the accent colour where the typ uses the name colour.
Presence and style are separate decisions, and asserting only presence missed
both — my previous test checked that Navy SHOWS a title, never how.

Added title_emphasised and caption_uses_name_colour to LetterDocxStyle, both
read off each typ, so the styling now travels with the layout the same way the
feature list does.

The new test asserts the styling rather than the presence: Refined uppercases
and tracks the role line, Navy does neither. Verified to fail against the
hardcoded version.

head_commit.message:
feat: add the cologne navy resume template and a shared navy letter layout (#953)

* feat: add the cologne navy resume template and a shared navy letter layout

Ports the supplied Cologne Navy design into the Typst backend as a 13th
template, plus a fourth cover-letter layout in matching styling.

Three of the brief's assumptions did not hold against this codebase, and each
changed the work:

Carlito is ALREADY bundled, and `FontFamily::Calibri` already resolves to it in
Typst — the metric-compatible substitution the brief asks for is the repo's
existing convention, so the "check whether it's bundled, add it if not" step was
already satisfied.

Letter templates are NOT per resume template. There are three shared layouts
behind a `LetterLayout` enum, chosen independently of the resume template. So
this adds a FOURTH shared layout, offered to every template and inheriting
whichever palette is active — a Regent user selecting Navy gets Regent's
burgundy. Confirmed as the intent before building it.

`base` as a per-template size option conflicts with the model here: `_scale.typ`
is a locked shared house scale and the only per-template knobs that reach a
template are page size, accent, lang, ats and has_photo. The design's
"everything is a multiple of base" property is preserved as ratios off body_pt;
adding a real size option would be a pipeline change across all thirteen
templates, not a template addition.

The reference also consumed its own rich schema (skills groups, project
stack/links, footnotes rows). This repo has ONE generic IR every template
shares, so what is ported is the LOOK, not the schema — the same way meridian
and throughline style identical `sections[].blocks[]` differently. Nothing was
invented and no section dropped.

DEVIATION worth reading: the brief's 0.14em name / 0.18em heading tracking makes
the PDF text extract letter-by-letter — the name came back as
"À LVA R O   È S P O S I T O" and headings as "S U M M A R Y". For a
job-application tool that is an ATS-unreadable name, not a cosmetic issue.
Reduced to 0.06em / 0.10em, the widest values that still extract, and inside the
0.03–0.10em band every other template here already uses. Caught by the
every-template extraction test, which fails at the brief's values.

Also fixes three stale counts found while wiring this up, all unnoticed because
the generators are ignored by CI: the cover-preview generator asserted 10 files
against a 12-entry list (so it could not be run at all), the showcase banner
hardcoded COLS=12 and panicked with an out-of-bounds pixel write on a 13th cell,
and both printed hardcoded counts in their success messages. All now derive from
the canonical list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop the navy letter rendering as banded in docx, and unhardcode its tracking

Five review findings.

The DOCX letter renderer branched on a single `is_refined` boolean, so Navy fell
into the else and inherited BANDED's decoration — the shaded header band and the
short rule footer, neither of which the Navy design has. The same export
therefore produced a Navy PDF and a Banded DOCX. Split out `is_banded` for the
two branches that are genuinely Banded-only, and gave Navy its own centred
letterhead over a bottom rule, which is the parser-safe echo of the .typ. The
branches Navy legitimately shares with Banded (uppercase name, bolded
date/recipient) stay on `!is_refined` rather than being duplicated.

Navy had no DOCX coverage at all. It now joins the three enumerated loops
(font-size ceiling, letterhead-less, subject-line) and the distinct-bytes test,
where the load-bearing pair is Navy vs Banded — that assertion fails against the
old boolean.

`cologne_navy.typ` set fonts as bare strings while every other template, its own
PR sibling included, uses a fallback tuple. Given fallbacks are how the bundled
Carlito is reached in the first place, that was a real gap, not a style nit.

`heading_tracking: 0.18` in the registry was both dead and wrong — the template
hardcoded 0.10em. The template now reads the field and the registry says 0.10,
so the source of truth is single and the extraction constraint is recorded where
someone changing it will look.

And the tier-badge test asserted only an aggregate count, which would still pass
if a different card supplied the eighth ATS badge and cologne-navy were missing
entirely. Added an assertion naming the card.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: route every navy docx branch by feature, not by "not refined"

The review was right that my first pass was partial, and finishing it found two
more mismatches it had not named.

I split only the header band and the footer rule and left the rest binary, so
Navy still lost Refined's role line and subject caption and still inherited
Banded's bolding. My own commit message claimed Navy "legitimately shares the
bolded date/recipient" with Banded — that was wrong, and checking
letter_navy.typ would have shown it: its emit-date-block and
emit-recipient-block carry no `weight: "bold"`, unlike letter_banded.typ's. I
asserted a justification instead of reading the template I had just written.

Replaced the boolean with per-FEATURE flags derived from what each `.typ`
actually renders — shows_title, shows_subject_caption, bolds_addressing — so a
future layout has to state its behaviour rather than inherit Banded's by
default.

Two further mismatches found while auditing the remaining branches:

The contact line was right-aligned unconditionally, so Navy's centred letterhead
was centred name over a right-aligned contact.

And the letterhead rule sat on the NAME paragraph, drawing a line between the
name and its own contact line. letter_navy.typ rules under the whole block
(name → title → contact), so it belongs on the contact paragraph.

The new test asserts the FEATURES rather than "differs from Banded" — no shaded
band, centred letterhead, fewer bold runs than Banded. "Differs from Banded"
passes as soon as one branch is split, which is exactly how the first pass
looked complete. Verified to fail against the single-boolean version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: make each letter layout state its docx style instead of inheriting

Third review round on this function, so patching a fourth branch was the wrong
answer.

The finding was real: the no-profile FALLBACK contact path still right-aligned
Navy with no rule, while the profile-backed path centred it and ruled it. The
same letter rendered differently depending on whether a ContactProfile happened
to be attached.

The cause is structural, not a missed line. A single `is_refined` boolean with
everything else falling through to Banded meant adding a layout inherited
Banded's look by DEFAULT, and each review round found a different survivor:
round one the header band and footer rule, round two the title, subject caption
and bolding, round three this contact path.

Replaced it with a `LetterDocxStyle` filled in per layout — uppercase name, name
size bonus, header band, centred letterhead, title, subject caption, addressing
bold, header rule, footer rule, signature gap, and the two spacing values. Every
call site reads a field, and both contact paths call one `contact_align()` so
they cannot drift apart again. A new layout now fails to compile until someone
states what it does.

The test was weak in the same way the code was: `contains("center")` passed
while the fallback contact was still right-aligned, because centring the NAME
alone satisfied it. It now counts centred and right-aligned paragraphs and
requires at least two centred — verified to fail against the pre-fix fallback.

Behaviour for Classic, Refined and Banded is unchanged; their table entries were
read off the existing branches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: style navy's docx title and caption from its own typ, not refined's

Both findings are the same defect as the last three rounds, one level down: the
style struct made each feature's PRESENCE layout-aware and left its STYLING
hardcoded to Refined's.

So Navy rendered the role line accent-coloured, uppercased and letter-spaced
while letter_navy.typ puts it in the muted date colour, plain case, untracked;
and the subject caption in the accent colour where the typ uses the name colour.
Presence and style are separate decisions, and asserting only presence missed
both — my previous test checked that Navy SHOWS a title, never how.

Added title_emphasised and caption_uses_name_colour to LetterDocxStyle, both
read off each typ, so the styling now travels with the layout the same way the
feature list does.

The new test asserts the styling rather than the presence: Refined uppercases
and tracks the role line, Navy does neither. Verified to fail against the
hardcoded version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix: stop squashing the embeddings checkbox, and unnest the provider row button (#952)

* fix: stop squashing the embeddings checkbox, and unnest the provider row button

Both reported off a screenshot of the shipped UI, plus one found by the log
bridge. All three are things no test covered because nobody had looked.

The two embeddings toggles looked like different controls. One cause: the row is
`justify-between` with no gap and the `<input>` had no `shrink-0`. Semantic
scoring's one-line description leaves slack so it renders correctly; the longer
auto-index description fills the row, so the copy butts against the checkbox AND
flexbox compresses the input below its own h-4 w-4. Not a different checkbox —
a squashed one. Fixed on both rows so a future copy change to either cannot
bring it back.

`ProviderRow` wrapped its header in a `<Button>` and nested the "test key"
`<Button>` inside it: invalid DOM, and clicking test-key also toggled the row's
expand. React had been reporting it as "<button> cannot contain a nested
<button>" into devtools where nobody saw it; it only became visible once the
renderer console bridge started writing to the log file. Converted to the
repo's existing `role="button"` row pattern (see NotificationBell), which keeps
Enter/Space activation without the nesting.

Writing the tests surfaced a third: the semantic-scoring checkbox had no
aria-label. Added.

Asserted on classes rather than geometry — jsdom reports zero width/height, so a
computed-size assertion would have passed against the broken markup. Both layout
tests were verified to fail against the shipped version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop the test-key click from also expanding the provider row

Flagged by both the pre-push gate and the CI review, and they were right about
something I had claimed in the PR body but not actually done.

Unnesting the row's <button> fixed the invalid DOM, but not the behaviour it
caused: the inner "test key" click still BUBBLES to the row's handler, so
testing a key kept toggling the row's expand. Markup-only fixes leave that
intact. Enter/Space is worse — a focused <button> fires a native click too, so
the keydown reached the row's handler whose preventDefault() could suppress the
button's own activation.

Guarded with stopPropagation on both onClick and onKeyDown, the same pattern
ApplicationRow already uses for its note chip and status dropdown.

Tests now pin the behaviour rather than the markup: test-key does not expand,
the row itself still expands (the differential — a guard that swallowed
everything would pass the first assertion while breaking the row), and the row
stays keyboard-activatable. Verified to fail with the guard removed.

Also corrected the nesting assertion: it used getAllByRole('button'), which
matches the role="button" row too, so it flagged the legitimate real-button-
inside-role-button-row pattern. It now checks actual <button> elements, which
is what React's rule is about.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
